content.text: {"decisions":[{"candidate_id":"E13","decision":"shortlist","major_issues":[],"rationale":"This candidate remains defensible for researcher consideration because its stated question is appropriately bounded: whether a TEA/TEOA CO/H2 difference in the P01 family survives tighter composition normalization with attribution controls. The design is anchored by direct system evidence for the CoCl2+bpy/g-C3N4/MeCN:H2O/TEOA family, includes TEA as a related donor option, and now contains internal Ar and no-amine controls that bound carbon-product attribution and additive necessity. Importantly, the card does not claim that equalized recipe logic makes TEA and TEOA chemically equivalent, and it explicitly limits interpretation of any collapse in donor difference to reduced compatibility with a strong medium-dominant account rather than proof of a specific proton-management mechanism. Residual multi-property confounding remains, but it is acknowledged and kept within the inference limits rather than hidden.","evidence_support":"direct","inference_validity":"adequate_for_stated_question","candidate_value":"retain","implementation_readiness":"ready_for_researcher_planning","resource_level":"low_cost","prior_issue_resolution":"No change from the prior favorable assessment. Prior issue 1 remains resolved because the card explicitly states that normalization cannot erase intrinsic TEA/TEOA chemical differences. Prior issue 2 remains resolved through added Ar controls and a no-amine condition. Prior issue 3 remains resolved because support/refute language stays narrowly bounded and does not overclaim mechanism from selectivity collapse. Decision is unchanged because the card still matches its controls to its stated inference."},{"candidate_id":"E14","decision":"revise","major_issues":["Signal assignment remains substantially ambiguous in a mixed Co-bpy/g-C3N4 suspension, so donor-dependent isotope-sensitive features may still reflect support, solvent, scattering, or cobalt-speciation changes rather than the intended hydrogen-coupled states.","D2O substitution remains a multi-property perturbation, so donor-dependent isotope responses cannot cleanly separate proton-management effects from other solvent-isotope consequences.","The exact spectroscopic implementation is still pilot-defined rather than fully specified, so cross-group comparability depends on successful preliminary mode selection and quality thresholds."],"rationale":"This is still a potentially valuable specialist characterization screen, but not yet a shortlist item. The card improved by fixing the logic to one predefined operando or near-operando mode per execution, by adding donor-free reference, and by narrowing interpretation to hydrogen-coupled observables rather than unique intermediate identities. Those changes materially reduce prior overreach. However, the core inferential problem remains: in this heterogeneous suspension, reproducible isotope-sensitive spectral differences would still be difficult to assign confidently, and D2O changes more than proton transfer. The candidate therefore has research value as a pilot-led mechanistic screen, but its conclusions remain assignment-limited and need careful revision before stronger researcher planning.","evidence_support":"transfer_with_limits","inference_validity":"needs_revision","candidate_value":"conditional","implementation_readiness":"pilot_needed","resource_level":"specialist","prior_issue_resolution":"No decision change from the prior review. Prior issue 1 was only partially resolved: the card now restricts assignments to candidate hydrogen-coupled features and includes donor-free reference, but unique signal assignment remains unresolved. Prior issue 2 was only partially resolved because the card acknowledges D2O as a multi-property perturbation but cannot remove that confounding. Prior issue 3 was partly resolved by requiring one fixed mode and pilot-set quality thresholds, yet exact implementation still depends on pilot success. The unchanged revise decision is therefore still justified."},{"candidate_id":"E15","decision":"shortlist","major_issues":[],"rationale":"This remains a strong bounded characterization candidate. The question is descriptive and well matched to the controls: whether TEA and TEOA produce different detectable CO2-responsive solution-state signatures in matched P01 medium before illumination or after dark equilibration. The design includes within-donor inert versus CO2 contrasts, a no-amine background, and allowance for component-minus-one references. It also explicitly states that any donor-specific signal would indicate association only, not catalytic active-state identity or causal mechanism. The clarified-supernatant fallback is transparently labeled as a transfer limitation rather than treated as equivalent chemistry. Because the card asks only what the proposed measurements can support, no major issue blocks shortlist.","evidence_support":"transfer_with_limits","inference_validity":"adequate_for_stated_question","candidate_value":"retain","implementation_readiness":"pilot_needed","resource_level":"moderate","prior_issue_resolution":"No change from the prior shortlist assessment. Earlier concerns remain addressed: inert references, no-amine background, reproducibility checks, and explicit limits against overassigning adduct identity or catalytic relevance are still present. No new substantive issue appears on this card, so the unchanged shortlist decision remains appropriate."},{"candidate_id":"E16","decision":"revise","major_issues":["The bounded replacement arm still depends on an unspecified pre-screened non-donor base whose coordination, ionic-strength, solvation, or side-reactivity effects could confound interpretation beyond proton-management changes.","The rescue logic remains intrinsically non-exclusive: partial rescue by the replacement base would be only descriptive medium evidence, while failure to rescue would not exclude proton-management contributions because sacrificial donation is not reproduced.","The E16G03 versus E16G04 comparison remains explicitly confounded by simultaneous change in amine presence and base presence, so it cannot support mechanistic ranking beyond a weak descriptive bound."],"rationale":"This candidate is improved and worth retaining conditionally, but revise remains the correct decision. The omission arm is useful because it tests whether an amine is functionally necessary under the P01 baseline, and the direct TEA/TEOA arm remains a valid multifunctional-additive comparison. The revision also strengthened the replacement arm by requiring pilot screening for low blank reactivity, mixture compatibility, and measurable bulk acid-base shift, and by permitting that arm to be dropped if no suitable base exists. Even so, the core inferential limitation remains substantial: a non-donor base is not an amine surrogate in this photocatalytic context, and any movement in activity or selectivity can arise from several medium changes unrelated to the target interpretation. The candidate is therefore useful as a bounded intervention screen, but still needs cautious framing rather than shortlist status.","evidence_support":"transfer_with_limits","inference_validity":"needs_revision","candidate_value":"conditional","implementation_readiness":"details_needed","resource_level":"low_cost","prior_issue_resolution":"No decision change from the prior review. Prior issue 1 remains only partly resolved because pilot screening now constrains base choice, but the replacement species is still unspecified and potentially confounding. Prior issue 2 remains unresolved in principle: rescue and non-rescue remain mechanistically non-exclusive, though the card now states this clearly. Prior issue 3 also remains, but the card now correctly labels the confounded comparison as descriptive only. The revise decision therefore stays unchanged."},{"candidate_id":"E17","decision":"shortlist","major_issues":[],"rationale":"This remains a well-bounded descriptive interaction map suited to the stated hypothesis. It asks whether the TEA/TEOA CO/H2 difference depends strongly on water fraction within the P01 family, using balanced donor comparisons at two pilot-selected MeCN/H2O settings that must remain operationally comparable. The design explicitly treats any donor-by-water interaction, collapse, or crossover as evidence for medium involvement rather than proof of a unique proton-relay or CO2-adduct mechanism. It also builds in practical comparability checks for phase behavior, common analytics, and matched handling. Because the question is descriptive and the inference is limited to donor-by-medium dependence, the candidate remains suitable for researcher consideration without major revision.","evidence_support":"transfer_with_limits","inference_validity":"adequate_for_stated_question","candidate_value":"retain","implementation_readiness":"ready_for_researcher_planning","resource_level":"low_cost","prior_issue_resolution":"No change from the prior favorable assessment. Earlier concerns about overclaiming remain addressed through explicit limitations, pilot selection of operationally comparable water settings, and descriptive treatment of any crossover. No new substantive issue appears, so shortlist remains justified on the unchanged card."},{"candidate_id":"E18","decision":"shortlist","major_issues":[],"rationale":"This remains a defensible descriptive covariate screen. The card now focuses on directly measured bulk descriptors that first pass a stability pilot in the actual medium, prioritizing one consistent acidity proxy and conductivity, and it repeatedly states that these are bulk covariates rather than direct measures of the local catalytic environment. The matched TEA/TEOA and H2O/D2O comparisons can therefore test whether donor-dependent catalytic differences co-vary with stable measurable medium descriptors, while keeping the conclusion descriptive instead of causal. The previously problematic overreach around CO2-uptake proxy has been removed from the core design, and the D2O arms are already bounded as isotope perturbations rather than single-factor mechanistic proof. With those limits preserved, no major issue blocks shortlist.","evidence_support":"transfer_with_limits","inference_validity":"adequate_for_stated_question","candidate_value":"retain","implementation_readiness":"pilot_needed","resource_level":"low_cost","prior_issue_resolution":"No change from the prior review that upgraded this card. Prior issue 1 remains resolved because the card explicitly limits itself to validated bulk measures and denies equivalence to the local catalytic environment. Prior issue 2 remains resolved by framing the study as a descriptive covariate screen rather than a causal proton-management test. Prior issue 3 remains resolved because the earlier CO2-uptake proxy is still excluded from the core readout set. The shortlist decision therefore remains appropriate on the unchanged revised card."}],"overall":"Shortlist E13, E15, E17, and E18; keep E14 and E16 as revise. The strongest candidates are the ones whose controls and conclusions are already matched to a bounded descriptive question inside the supplied P01 formulation family. E13 remains the best direct-system comparison because it combines anchored and normalized donor contrasts with Ar and no-amine attribution controls while explicitly avoiding overclaim that normalization makes TEA and TEOA equivalent. E15 and E17 remain strong because they ask descriptive questions that their measurements can actually answer: donor-dependent CO2-responsive solution-state signatures and donor-by-water interaction, respectively. E18 is also shortlist-worthy because it has been successfully narrowed to a bulk-covariate screen with validated descriptors rather than mechanistic proof. By contrast, E14 still suffers from signal-assignment ambiguity and multi-property isotope perturbation, and E16 still depends on a chemically underdetermined replacement-base arm whose rescue logic is intrinsically non-exclusive. Across the set, direct evidence mainly supports staying within the P01 recipe family, while most mechanistic rationale is transferred with clear limits from other cobalt or bipyridine-related systems. A sensible research sequence would therefore prioritize the shortlisted bounded screens first, then use the revise candidates only if those simpler comparisons justify more assignment-limited specialist follow-up."}
